title: Parameters, defaults, and return values
runtime: Modern evergreen browser or Node.js with ES modules. Run fragments in browser DevTools or a small .js file unless the example says otherwise.

objectives.text: Use default parameters for missing values.
Return useful results on every intended path.
Treat the signature as a small contract.

learningFlow: Explain the result in your own words

diagnostic.question: Can you explain the main purpose of parameters, defaults, and return values before reading?
diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: Parameters describe inputs
sections.body: Parameters are local names listed by the function; arguments are the values supplied by the caller. JavaScript allows missing and extra arguments, so a function should define which inputs are required. For many related options, an object parameter is often clearer than a long positional list.

sections.title: Defaults run for undefined
sections.body: A default parameter is used when the argument is omitted or explicitly undefined. It is not used for null, 0, false, or an empty string. A default expression is evaluated when the function is called, so it can use earlier parameters.

sections.title: return ends the function
sections.body: return immediately stops the function and gives a value to the caller. A function without an executed return produces undefined. When a function claims to calculate a result, make each valid path return the promised shape; accidental undefined values otherwise travel into later code.

sections.title: Inputs and outputs form a contract
sections.body: A reliable function makes its expectations visible: accepted input, returned value, possible mutation, and possible error. Validate at system boundaries, keep internal functions focused, and use examples that include normal, empty, and invalid input.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Parameters, defaults, and return values is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain parameters, defaults, and return values to a junior developer.
interviewQuestions.answer: Design clear parameters and arguments. Use default parameters for missing values. Return useful results on every intended path. Treat the signature as a small contract.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Show a small example and one common mistake.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using parameters, defaults, and return values behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which edge case would you test first?

interviewQuestions.question: Where can parameters, defaults, and return values affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.

commonMistakes.symptom: Code using parameters, defaults, and return values produces a surprising value.
commonMistakes.cause: The result was run before the value, type, scope, identity, or control flow was predicted.
commonMistakes.fix: Reduce the case, write the expected result, and apply the exact rule from the matching section.

commonMistakes.symptom: A learner copies syntax but cannot adapt it.
commonMistakes.cause: The example was memorized without explaining why it works.
commonMistakes.fix: Change the data and names, predict again, and explain which behavior must stay the same.

commonMistakes.symptom: A React problem is blamed on React immediately.
commonMistakes.cause: The underlying JavaScript behavior was not isolated first.
commonMistakes.fix: Reproduce the value or function behavior in a small JavaScript example, then reconnect it to the component.
